title: Marguerite and the Alibi
premise: Yara Yarrow, an insurance investigator with a photographic memory, is hired by a nervous client named Marguerite to prove that a murder has not yet happened — hers, predicted by a ledger of deaths she found hidden in her late husband's bookshop. As Yara decodes the ledger's cipher, he realizes it records not predictions but plans, and that Marguerite's 'family' of boarders each appear in its pages. The final entry names Yara himself. In the climax, Yara exposes the ledger's author — the shop's gentle handyman, who kills to keep his found family from scattering — and saves Marguerite, but must choose whether to report a man whose crimes were born of the same loneliness Yara has always carried.
about_author: Ansel Voss is the pen name of a former claims adjuster who spent eleven years reading other people's disasters and decided to start inventing his own. He writes mysteries about people who remember too much and belong too little.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. A pale, precise woman named Marguerite hires Yara to prove her murder hasn't happened yet, paying triple for discretion. She shows him a ledger of names and dates found sewn into her dead husband's bookshop sofa — the last date is next week. Yara, who memorizes everything but trusts no one, takes the case against his better judgment. Emotional beat: wary curiosity masking loneliness.

chapters.title: The House That Remembers
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. Investigating the bookshop and its upstairs boarders — a retired nurse, a drifting musician, a shy handyman named Oren — Yara finds the household unnervingly warm, a found family he aches to be part of. Cross-checking the ledger against old insurance files, he matches three past entries to unsolved local deaths. Emotional beat: belonging tempted against suspicion; the warmth starts to feel like a trap.

chapters.title: Every Name But Hers
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. Decoding the cipher, Yara discovers the ledger isn't prophecy — it's a kill list written in advance, and every death protected the household's fragile peace. The final two entries: Marguerite, who plans to sell the shop, and Yara, who knows too much. When Marguerite disappears on the ledger's appointed night, Yara races back through rain-slick streets. Emotional beat: dread crystallizing into resolve.

chapters.title: The Price of Staying
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. In the bookshop cellar, Yara confronts Oren, who confesses he killed to keep his family from dissolving — and offers Yara a place in it if he forgets what he remembers. Yara saves Marguerite, refuses the poisoned gift of belonging bought with blood, and turns Oren in, then stays on as the shop's new tenant anyway. Emotional beat: grief and grace; survival without surrender.
